title: 神経科学
subtitle: Neuroscience
educationalGoal: This course is intended for Brain Science majors. The goal of this course is to introduce students to the study of neuroscience. Students will learn fundamental information about cellular biology and the electrophysiological properties of neurons, neuroanatomy, psychopharmacology, and how the activity of neurons can yield sensory perception, motor control, and complex behavioral functions such as learning and motivation.
advice: We will explain the structure and function of neurons (nerve cells), which are the basic units of the brain and nervous system that produce our behavior, and the brain, which is an aggregate of them. We will explain the mechanism of the neural circuit that supports each process from the acceptance of various senses to the integrated processing in the brain and the production of behavior as motor output, including talks at the molecular level. In addition, we will explain the formation and plasticity of the nervous system involved in higher-order functions of the brain such as the development of the nervous system and learning and memory. Rather than simply setting the viewpoint to human behavior, we will learn concretely about their neural basis through neuroethology and comparative physiology, while contrasting with the behavior of other animals. We will accept questions from students at any time and proceed in an interactive lecture format.
requiredKnowledge: 基礎生物学や人体の構造と機能、細胞の構造と機能などで学んだ感覚、運動、行動を支える生理学的なしくみや、細胞、脳の働きなどの基本的な理解が求められる。

activityGoals.body: Explain the structure and function of nerves and brain.
Animal and human behavior can be explained as the function of the brain and nerves.
Explain the molecular cell mechanism of memory.
Explain the neural basis of long-term memory.
Explain the relationship between neurotransmitter structures and individuals (humans and mice).
